problemStatement.formal: question_part1 ∧ question_part2 where question_part1 = Set.Infinite {n | harmonicGCD n = 1} and question_part2 = Set.Infinite {n | harmonicGCD n > 1}
problemStatement.plain: Do both gcd(a_n, L_n) = 1 and gcd(a_n, L_n) > 1 occur for infinitely many n, where H_n = a_n/L_n?
whyMatters: Connects harmonic number arithmetic to transcendence theory via Schanuel's conjecture
Leading digit criterion links number-theoretic divisibility to base representations

proven: Part 2 (infinitely many n with gcd > 1) is trivially YES via Steinerberger/Wolstenholme
Divisibility characterization: p | gcd iff p | numerator of H_k where k = leading digit in base p
Concrete values: H_1 through H_6, L_1 through L_6 computed
Steinerberger applied to n=6,8,24 and family 2*3^k
open: Part 1: infinitely many n with gcd(a_n, L_n) = 1 (OPEN)
Exact asymptotics for count of n with gcd = 1
knownResults.goal: Formalize known results around the problem; Part 1 remains genuinely open

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: 48 theorems, 6 axioms, 0 sorries. Comprehensive harmonic number divisibility formalization with concrete H and L values, leading digit computations, Steinerberger applications, Wolstenholme theorem, and infinite family gcd>1 proof. leadingDigit_two_times_pow_three converted from axiom to theorem.
builtItems: prime_not_dvd_factorial_of_gt: prime larger than n does not divide n!
H_two through H_six: concrete harmonic number values
L_three through L_six: concrete LCM values
H_mul_L_nonneg, H_mul_L_eq_sum: algebraic properties of H*L product
Fixed dvd_L: proper inductive proof using Nat.dvd_lcm_left/right
leadingDigit_two_times_pow_three: proved from axiom (2*3^k has leading digit 2 in base 3)
insights: harmonicGCD is noncomputable, preventing native_decide on small_examples
Finset.dvd_fold_lcm does not exist in current Mathlib; use Nat.dvd_lcm_left/right with induction instead
Nat.Prime.dvd_factorial does not exist as a dot notation; need custom lemma
Steinerberger criterion axiom enables systematic applications to concrete cases via native_decide on leadingDigit
The family {2*3^k : k >= 1} provides infinitely many n with 3|gcd
mathlibGaps: No Nat.Prime.dvd_factorial or equivalent dot-notation lemma found
No Finset.dvd_fold_lcm for proving element divides fold of lcm
